# Tooltip

A popup that displays information related to an element when the element receives keyboard focus or the mouse hovers over it.

- **Import:** `import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider, TooltipTrigger } from "@kozmos-ds/react";`
- **Group:** Core
- **Platforms:** React, SwiftUI and Compose; linked to its Figma component through Code Connect.
- **Storybook:** <https://vodoco.github.io/kozmos-design-system/storybook/?path=/docs/overlay-tooltip--docs>

## Example

From its `Default` story.

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  ThemeProvider,
  Tooltip,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipTrigger,
} from "@kozmos-ds/react";

export function TooltipExample() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">
      <Tooltip>
        <TooltipTrigger asChild>
          <Button variant="outline">Hover me</Button>
        </TooltipTrigger>
        <TooltipContent>
          <p>Add to library</p>
        </TooltipContent>
      </Tooltip>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

## Tooltip

Its props are `TooltipPrimitive.TooltipProps`.

- `children`: `React.ReactNode`, optional.
- `open`: `boolean`, optional.
- `defaultOpen`: `boolean`, optional.
- `onOpenChange`: `(open: boolean) => void`, optional.
- `delayDuration`: `number`, optional, default `700`.

  The duration from when the pointer enters the trigger until the tooltip gets opened. This will
  override the prop with the same name passed to Provider.

- `disableHoverableContent`: `boolean`, optional, default `false`.

  When `true`, trying to hover the content will result in the tooltip closing as the pointer leaves the trigger.

## TooltipTrigger

Wrap the trigger when it is a disabled control, so the tooltip still works.

A disabled `<button>` fires no pointer events and cannot take focus, so a
tooltip attached directly to one is silently dead — and the tooltip that
matters most is the one saying _why_ a control is unavailable. Pass
`disabled` and the trigger becomes a focusable wrapper around the control,
which is the element Radix then listens on.

`tabIndex={0}` is the part that is easy to miss. Adding pointer handlers to a
plain wrapper looks like it works, because hovering does; but focus never
arrives, since the disabled child cannot emit it and a bare `<span>` cannot
receive it. A reason a keyboard user cannot reach is not a reason. The
wrapper deliberately takes a tab stop the disabled control gave up.

It forwards its ref to `HTMLButtonElement`. Its props are `Omit<TooltipPrimitive.TooltipTriggerProps & React.RefAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "ref"> & { disabled?: boolean }`.

- `disabled`: `boolean`, optional, default `false`.
- `asChild`: `boolean`, optional.
- `children`: `ReactNode`, optional.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).

## TooltipContent

It forwards its ref to `HTMLDivElement`. Its props are `Omit<TooltipPrimitive.TooltipContentProps & React.RefAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "ref"> & { portalContainer?: React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof TooltipPrimitive.Portal>["container"] }`.

- `portalContainer`: `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof TooltipPrimitive.Portal>["container"]`, optional.

  Defaults to the owning ThemeProvider; without a provider, remains inline.

- `aria-label`: `string`, optional.

  A more descriptive label for accessibility purpose

- `asChild`: `boolean`, optional.
- `forceMount`: `true`, optional.

  Used to force mounting when more control is needed. Useful when
  controlling animation with React animation libraries.

- `onEscapeKeyDown`: `DismissableLayerProps['onEscapeKeyDown']`, optional.

  Event handler called when the escape key is down.
  Can be prevented.

- `onPointerDownOutside`: `DismissableLayerProps['onPointerDownOutside']`, optional.

  Event handler called when the a `pointerdown` event happens outside of the `Tooltip`.
  Can be prevented.

- `side`: `Side`, optional.
- `sideOffset`: `number`, optional, default `4`.
- `align`: `Align`, optional.
- `alignOffset`: `number`, optional.
- `arrowPadding`: `number`, optional.
- `avoidCollisions`: `boolean`, optional.
- `collisionBoundary`: `Boundary | Boundary[]`, optional.
- `collisionPadding`: `number | Partial<Record<Side, number>>`, optional.
- `sticky`: `'partial' | 'always'`, optional.
- `hideWhenDetached`: `boolean`, optional.
- `updatePositionStrategy`: `'optimized' | 'always'`, optional.
- `children`: `ReactNode`, optional.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).

## TooltipProvider

Its props are `TooltipPrimitive.TooltipProviderProps`.

- `children`: `React.ReactNode`, **required**.
- `delayDuration`: `number`, optional, default `700`.

  The duration from when the pointer enters the trigger until the tooltip gets opened.

- `skipDelayDuration`: `number`, optional, default `300`.

  How much time a user has to enter another trigger without incurring a delay again.

- `disableHoverableContent`: `boolean`, optional, default `false`.

  When `true`, trying to hover the content will result in the tooltip closing as the pointer leaves the trigger.
